messages:
olivia: FYI we just got a high-sev from a EU customer — requests suddenly 5xxing and showing long tails. They say some requests are routing to us-west which adds ~300ms and breaks downstream auth/webhooks :rotating_light:

kevin: Can you paste example request IDs and timeframe? Any correlation with deploys or config changes?

olivia: Happened ~10:24-10:46 UTC. sample IDs: r-0a1b2c3d, r-0f9e8d7c. Customer trace shows initial egress to eu-west, health-check triggered failover, then traffic moved to us-west. They also saw some 401s and a billing spike.

sre-bot: [alert] region-health-check: eu-west marked UNHEALTHY at 2026-03-17T10:23:10Z by probe-service (status=403).

maria: Repro steps from support side:
1) curl -H "X-Client-ID: cust-123" -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:52.28.10.5
2) we got 403 from probe-auth-proxy then subsequent request went to us-west:

$ curl -v -H 'X-Client-ID: cust-123' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ping
> GET /v1/ping HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< content-type: application/json
< {"error":"probe auth token invalid"}

Followed by:
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ping --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:13.34.20.7
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK

olivia: Customer says billing shows double-counted short-lived sessions when fallback happens. They lost SLA for a regionally pinned workload.

alan: I rolled out the probe-auth token tightening for health probes 2h ago to address noisy probes. The change made the probe service require a scoped token; the rollout included a config that defaults to strict validation. Looks like some probes (especially edge NAT/old agents) are still using the legacy token and get 403. Health-check treats non-200 as unhealthy, flips routing.

kevin: That matches. If probes are 403 we mark region down and smart-routing will failover. We should not treat 403 from probe-auth as a hard failure until probes are updated.

jess: Quick checks I ran:
- rctl probe status --region eu-west -> returning 403 from auth proxy for ~40% of probes since 10:20
- rctl routes show-policy api.redwood.ai -> fallback-policy=region-preference with cross-region-fallback enabled

jess: Immediate mitigation options:
- rollback the probe-auth change (fast but broad), OR
- flip probe-service to accept legacy tokens for a rolling window (safer), OR
- change health-check policy to treat 403 as HUN? (not ideal)

kevin: Prefer accepting legacy tokens temporarily and then schedule a staged enforcement with a hard cutoff. Also disable cross-region fallback for region-pinned customers to avoid user-visible reroutes during this window.

alan: I can flip the accept-legacy flag in probe config now. Doing:

# on probe-config-cluster
kubectl set env deployment/probe-service ACCEPT_LEGACY_TOKENS=true --namespace=platform || true

alan: Pushed. Waiting for rollout.

sre-bot: [info] probe-service deployment updated by alan at 2026-03-17T10:31:02Z.

maria: After Alan's flip, customer retried at 10:33 and got 200s in eu-west again. They report lower latency and billing stabilized.

jess: Next steps (post-mitigation):
- roll out probe agent update to customers/edge nodes with new token (track 7d adoption)
- change health-check semantics to ignore 403 specifically for probe-auth errors (add explicit code mapping)
- add a short-circuit in routing: do not trigger cross-region failover solely on probe 403 unless corroborated by >=3 probe types (http+tcp+kv)
- add alerting that notifies on a sudden spike in probe 403% so we can catch this earlier

kevin: I'll open a follow-up ticket in eng-sre backlog to do the health-check semantics + routing guard. Alan, can you revert the strict enforcement PR or add rollout notes? We should also notify account managers for impacted customers.

alan: I'll add rollout notes and a revert PR ready if adoption doesn't hit 90% in 24h. Also added temporary region policy to prevent cross-region fallback for pinned customers.

olivia: Thanks — I've emailed the customer update and CC'd AM. Closing for now, will reopen if we see reoccurrence. :white_check_mark:
